findings.target: reference independent_reference.py run(): saved_primary_status adapter; primary run_primary.py output status
findings.observed_defect: The reference originally required saved primary status PASS, while the actual primary source writes PASS_SCOPED on zero failures.
findings.impact: The planned reference run would necessarily record a metadata FAIL even after a successful primary run.
findings.minimum_correction: Require the exact primary API status PASS_SCOPED in the reference, without weakening any numerical or physical check.
findings.preservation: Original reference source and author record preserved at reference/revisions/R14_F01_before_status_adapter/ with actual bytes and matching SHA-256.
findings.closure_evidence: Reviewed exact one-line source diff PASS -> PASS_SCOPED. Final reference retains PASS_SCOPED. Preserved original source SHA afbaad924e5c38414bde0835c61a515a0952d97a736de49c397c31447ec1a27c; corrected intermediate SHA81b681a9641c3864108a8ec0310b6f71c765bd771833c7c80df474af65c85aba.

findings.observed_defect: A2048-character limit followed by Fraction(text) did not bound exponent expansion before the256-bit check. A short zero-valued exponent spelling could request a huge10**exp allocation before reduction.
findings.evidence: Read actual /usr/lib/python3.12/fractions.py string parser: exponent integer conversion precedes10**exp and the caller's post-conversion bit check. No huge-exponent value was executed.
findings.impact: The stated finite input-parser work boundary could be bypassed before an eventual reduced-value/bit-domain decision, including for a mathematically zero scalar.
findings.minimum_correction: Check bounded ASCII signed-integer or signed p/q syntax before integer/Fraction conversion. Keep scalar256bit and input2048character bounds; use separate bounded saved-output parsing in the reference.
findings.actual_correction: Production uses ASCII fullmatch before bounded int numerator/denominator conversion. Reference independently scans ASCII characters before int conversion, caps saved text at10000characters and parsed components at6000digits, then checks reduced16384bit saved values; public input remains2048characters/256bits. Decimal/exponent/whitespace scientific input spellings are explicitly unsupported.
findings.metadata_adapter: The frozen numeric-policy literal1e-80 is checked by exact string equality rather than the scientific rational parser. This narrow adapter was verified in the final diff.
findings.preservation: Actual pre-edit production snapshot9/9 files and pre-F02/F03 reference source/author record bytes matched their recorded SHA-256 identities.
findings.numerical_input_delta: None: all31 valid case objects and original FIXTURE_SOURCE bytes are unchanged; all43 original guard objects are retained exactly. Three invalid lexical guards raise the total to46.

findings.target: production serializable() and standalone execution conversion policy; reference saved-value parser/output
findings.observed_defect: The current Python3.12.14 process default integer-string digit limit was4300, but accepted16384-bit derived numerator/denominator components can need4933decimal digits. The original serializer delegated directly to str(Fraction).
findings.impact: Some values inside the declared derived arithmetic domain could fail decimal output conversion. This was a general finite API defect, not a claim that the31 fixed cases had produced such a value.
findings.minimum_correction: Use a finite process-local conversion limit large enough for16384-bit components and bounded rational text; preserve separate public input limits. An unlimited zero setting is unnecessary.
findings.actual_correction: Dedicated R14 production core configures finite6000 at import, run_case entry and outer serialization; each Fraction is derived-bit checked and output text capped at10000characters. The standalone reference sets6000 in main, bounds saved text and records the effective policy. Neither source disables the limit.
findings.authored_check: Primary now serializes and parses a rational whose reduced numerator and denominator both have16384bits, checks the exact roundtrip,10000character bound and runtime6000 policy, and stores only its text length/SHA in the check detail.
findings.preservation: Actual pre-edit production snapshot11/11 files and pre-F02/F03 reference source/author record were preserved with matching SHA-256 identities.

Endpoint, right-left-limit and actual-right candidates are distinguished. Restricted rootbox hulls and midpoint witnesses use stored cubic coefficients; exact gap and dyadic expansion are separate. Both local and aggregated exact gap invariants are checked.

Positive Taylor96 term/moment floor-ceil updates, conservative exponential tail, negative-z reciprocal-exp/reversed moments and d=0 beta reduction match the proof. The tighter polynomial endpoint propagates onward; whole E separately uses exact R-sup upper and positive ge coefficient hull.

Scientific rational addition/subtraction/multiplication/division routes through the new16384-bit derived check. No older8192-bit helper is imported. Fixed128-bit dyadic integer loops and degree96 tail arithmetic are bounded separately; work count caps do not replace bit checks. F02/F03 now bound textual input/output conversion explicitly. Successful90CPU/120wall execution still requires the actual run.
